answer: A farm faking 549 aliases needs 549 separate fixture records, each built over years, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. Bandy club membership with fixture participation record is the check: fixtures played for one club season after season. The kernel check is what stops the copy-paste farm: The record is checked live against the issuer each epoch, and a missing or revoked entry loses the seat. The knoll record is public, the atlas cost is per identity, and 549 aliases cost 549 times one honest seat.
